newsitem.title: FRANCE: Elf Antar workers begin one-day strikes.
newsitem.headline: Elf Antar workers begin one-day strikes.

text.p: Distribution workers at Elf Aquitaine began carrying out a promise to disrupt three oil refineries on Wednesday, a company spokesman said.
Staff at Elf subsidiary Elf Antar staged a 24-hour strike at the 98,000 barrels per day (bpd) Grandpuits refinery near Paris from 0700 GMT, he said.
Other 24-hour strikes were planned at Elf's 128,000 bpd Feyzin refinery near Lyon and its 214,000 bpd Donges refinery in western France for Thursday, Elf and trade union spokesmen said.
Unions announced the disruption on Monday to protest against plans to shed 10 percent of Elf Antar's staff, or 330 jobs.
The strike is another headache for France's largest oil company, already affected by a blockade by striking French truckers. But the two disputes are not related, Elf said.
Truckers protesting about pay and conditions were preventing all but one French refinery loading fuel into road tankers on Wednesday, an oil industry spokewoman said earlier.
The transport strike was expected to start forcing refineries to cut output soon, especially in southern France, she said.
An Elf spokesman said he knew of no immediate plans to cut production besides brief stoppages caused by the Antar strike.
